races.title: State House, District 60
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Amanda Cook
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 60 since November 2025, when she was appointed to replace Cecil Brockman. Former dance teacher in Winston-Salem/Forsyth and Guilford County schools, founder of the nonprofit The Teacher's Edge, and High Point at-large city council member elected in 2023.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by State Rep. Tracy Clark (D), Carolina Federation PAC, Center for Freethought Equality and Work For Democracy, among others listed on Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: Her birth city is not stated in the pages found; they say only that she was born in 1982 and grew up in Columbia, SC. No records of bills she sponsored or other actions in office were found. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, immigration or H-1B, policing pay and pensions, or gun laws. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so her stated positions come only from her campaign site's issues page. Her 2022 survey answers were about school board service and are not used here.

local.label: Roots 40: She grew up in Columbia, SC, and moved to North Carolina in 2005 for college at UNCG, about 21 years of living here as an adult, working in Forsyth and Guilford county schools and serving on the High Point council.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Taught for about 13 years (2008-2021) in Winston-Salem/Forsyth and Guilford County schools, founded the nonprofit The Teacher's Edge in 2020, and was elected to the High Point City Council at-large in 2023. She has held the NC House seat since November 2025 by appointment and was elected to it in 2026.
qual.why: She has local elected office and a short stretch of state legislative service, plus nonprofit founding and management experience. She has no law or budget career and little time in the legislature, which puts her in the middle band. Her council committee seats and advisory board roles were not counted.

cands.name: Joseph Perrotta
cands.bio: Republican from High Point, North Carolina. Business owner and president per Ballotpedia, with a past career in information technology and field operations at large companies including AOL, AT&T and Mattress Firm. Ran for NC House District 60 in 2024 and 2026. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: Joseph Perrotta has never held public office, so there is no record of votes or official actions. We found no independent news coverage of him. We found nothing on his positions on guns, abortion, school choice, teacher pay, foreign land ownership or growth and land conservation. We could not confirm the name or details of the business he owns, or which Fortune 500 jobs he held and when. His claims come from his own candidate surveys.

local.label: Roots 80: Born in Bristol, CT, he says his family moved to North Carolina in 1993 during his freshman year of high school, and he graduated from Southwest Guilford High School.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Business owner and president (per Ballotpedia). Worked in information technology and field operations for large companies; as a Field Operations Supervisor at Mattress Firm he says he managed about $100 million in inventory across 80 distribution centers. Store manager at a cookie retailer early in his career. No elected office or legislative or policy work found.
qual.why: Management and business experience puts him in the middle range, but there is no legislative, policy or budget work and no office held, so he scores below the high range.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Said in his 2026 Ballotpedia survey that AI data centers will bring many jobs and that he supports evaluating each one separately so electricity and water costs aren't passed to residents. He did not call for a ban or moratorium.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Said in his 2026 Ballotpedia survey that he supports limiting how often local commissioners can reassess property values and raise property taxes.

workers-first.evidence: Said in his 2024 Ballotpedia survey that he would work to keep illegal immigrants from being relocated to district neighborhoods, adhere to existing immigration law and strengthen border security with new legislation.

back-police-order.evidence: Said in his 2024 Ballotpedia survey that he would fully support law enforcement officers and fight for their ability to take criminals off the streets.
